content.text: I will get you the data asap. I just got it and have a urgent issues that need to addressing today. I will get it to you sometime this week.

As for your questions:
- Yes, the letter is considered disciplinary. It is a formal written warning. The reassignment falls under management rights and is not looped into the disciplinary case. Only the letter is disciplinary. If they were reassigning you as part of disciplinary action, we would have a major issue. But management has not done this. 
- We do not always grieve discipline if it follows progressive discipline. In this case it did. In order to file a grievance there has to be a contractual violation. The company is within its rights to discipline appropriately and did not skip or misuse progressive discipline steps or violate just cause. 
- I would write the response asap. There is no deadline but you don't want a ton of time to go by. Generally, I take a look at this to make sure they are sticking to the  facts and are neutral. I would gladly do this for you, if you like.
I am not involved in the process of applying for that unpaid leave. Based on the language it seems you would go to management for this.

On Mon, Aug 31, 2020 at 5:57 AM Anthony Fenech <anthonyfenech@hotmail.com> wrote:
Hello Stevie,
Thanks for getting me that wage information a couple weeks ago, it was helpful. Whenever you receive those updated numbers and can pass them along, let me know.
After speaking with them more, I have a some questions about certain situations in Guild contract:
- Was the letter I received from Peter on Aug. 13 considered discipline?

My understanding is that it was - the discipline is essentially a write-up or "written warning." Though it wasn't explicitly stated that the discipline was "re-assignment from the Tigers beat," it doesn't need to be - management can change a reporter's assignment for essentially any reason.

- If the letter I received from Peter on Aug. 13 is considered discipline, then under Article XV, Section B, "A grievance shall be submitted within fourteen (14) calendar days [twenty-one] (21) days in the case of discipline or discharges] following the date on which the aggrieved employee or the Union knew or should have known of its occurrence."
Based on that, 21 days would be Sept. 3, right?

- After I received the letter, you mentioned that I have the opportunity to submit a written response to also be included in my file. Is there a deadline for submitting this, similar to the aforementioned deadline?

Also, I received my employee file from the company this weekend and it did not include the letter I received from Peter on Aug. 13. I requested it on Aug. 20, so maybe it's not updated. But I let Peter know I was requesting it, so I'd assume he would make sure the letter was in there.

- To your knowledge, what is the process for submitting a request for an unpaid leave of absence? My interpretation of the Guild contract is that based on my service time, I am eligible to be granted a leave of absence without pay for up to six months, provided that there aren't too many employees on leave. It says "by agreement with the Publisher," so I'm looking for information on any protocol involved: Do I go directly to management with this?

Administrative Officer
Newspaper Guild of Detroit
928-380-0286
